name: Pesarattu
subtitle: a green whole-moong crepe topped with raw onion, ginger and chilli

ingredients.note: just enough for crispness; more and it stops being pesarattu
4 ground into the batter, 2 finely chopped for the topping

ingredients.qty: 1 large, very finely chopped, for topping

prepNotes: Soak the whole moong and rice together for 6 hours or overnight. The skins must be soft enough to grind smooth without being removed.
Pesarattu batter is not fermented — grind it and cook straight away, which makes it a good same-morning breakfast.
Chop the onion for the topping as fine as you can and keep it dry, ready beside the stove.

steps.text: Drain the soaked moong and rice and grind with the whole green chillies, ginger, 1 tsp of the cumin and the salt to a smooth batter, adding water gradually.
steps.tip: Aim for a batter a shade thinner than dosa batter — it should coat the ladle but pour freely.

steps.text: Stir in the remaining cumin seeds whole, for texture.
Heat the tawa over medium-high, then rub it with half an onion dipped in oil.
steps.tip: The onion-rub seasons the pan and stops sticking better than oil alone.

steps.text: Lower the heat slightly, pour a ladleful in the centre and spread outward in a slow spiral to a 22cm round.
Scatter a generous tablespoon of chopped onion, chilli and coriander over the wet surface and press it down with the ladle.
steps.tip: Press the topping in while the surface is still wet or it falls off when you fold the crepe.

steps.text: Drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge and cook 3 minutes until the base is crisp and speckled brown and the edges curl away.
Flip and cook 1 minute only, just to set the onion.
steps.tip: One minute on the onion side. Longer and the topping burns while the crepe goes leathery.

steps.text: Fold in half and serve hot with allam pachadi or a plain coconut chutney.

storage: Eat immediately; pesarattu softens as it sits. The ground batter keeps 2 days refrigerated but the green dulls to olive — stir well and use within that window.
